city_center.name: Downtown San Antonio / River Walk
city_center.landmark: The Alamo (Mission San Antonio de Valero, 1718) and the cypress-lined River Walk along the San Antonio River
city_center.notes: San Antonio grew along the San Antonio River, where Spanish Franciscans built five missions between 1718 and 1731 -- now a UNESCO World Heritage Site; the River Walk is the downtown gathering water, lined with bald cypress. sources: San Antonio Missions NHS (nps.gov); Alamo / Mission San Antonio de Valero (smarthistory.org); River Walk (americanheritage.com).

featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: Tejano pan dulce sweetness + South Texas citrus and pecans; Spanish colonial mission stone

cultural_notes: Spanish Franciscans established five Catholic missions along the San Antonio River between 1718 and 1731 -- Valero (the Alamo), Concepcion, San Jose, San Juan, and Espada -- now inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (source: nps.gov San Antonio Missions NHS; visitsanantonio.com missions guide)

the missions blended Spanish and Indigenous traditions into the distinct culture of South Texas; farmlands, granaries, kilns, and still-working Spanish acequia irrigation survive at the mission complexes (source: nps.gov World Heritage Site article; nps.gov Spanish Influence in Texas)

H-E-B is headquartered in San Antonio and took more than 50% of the area grocery market in 2024, up from 47% in 2022 -- the strongest local-grocer loyalty of any Kodiak Texas market (source: axios.com H-E-B grows its market share in San Antonio; expressnews.com)

the River Walk's Spanish-colonial Christmas -- cobblestone walks, little bridges, majestic cypresses lit with colored lights and decorated water taxis -- is a signature civic winter ritual (source: americanheritage.com A Spanish Colonial Christmas in San Antonio)
